newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, Russia in row over NATO naval exercises.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, Russia in row over NATO naval exercises.

text.p: A top Ukrainian diplomat said on Tuesday that despite Moscow's objections Kiev was ready to host joint naval exercises with NATO countries in August in the Crimean peninsula.
"We will go ahead with the exercises and will continue efforts to convince Russia the exercises are not a bad thing," Deputy Foreign Minister Borys Hyduma said.
"Russia's fears that the exercises have anti-Russian, discriminatory aims are baseless," he told reporters.

The Sea Breeze-97 excercises are scheduled for August in the north-west part of the Crimean peninsula, which many Russians consider to be theirs although past Kremlin leader Nikita Khrushchev gave it to Ukraine as a gift in 1954.
Kiev will contribute 10 ships, several planes, and other forces to the exercises in which the United States, Britain, Germany, France, Italy, Greece, Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania will also take part.

Ukraine has invited Russia to take part in the exercises planned as part of NATO's Partnership for Peace programme, but Moscow has turned down the invitation. Albania and Georgia will take part as observers.
"The joint forces help people, establish order, and supply food. There is nothing provocative against Russia," Hudyma said.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Monday criticised NATO for the planned manoeuvres in Crimea, where three-quarters of its 2.7 million people are ethnic Russians, repeating statements that NATO expansion would threaten Moscow's security.

"How can we accept a military organisation acting around our borders, and openly at that?" Yeltsin said. "Why, against Russia's wishes, are they preparing to have exercises in the Crimea, in the Black Sea?"
Relations between Ukraine and Russia, far from warm, have been overshadowed by strife over division of the Black Sea Fleet and the terms of leasing the main base in Sevastopol.
The signing of a friendship treaty has been blocked for several years and Yeltsin has postponed Kiev visits six times.
President Leonid Kuchma recently called Russian policy towards Ukraine "aggressive" and said Moscow was "pushing Ukraine" towards NATO."

"Russia is an independent sovereign state and has a right to have its own position (on exercises). Russia's policy is aimed at stability, peace and cooperation," Russian ambassador to Kiev, Deputy Foreign Minister Yuri Dubinin, told reporters.
"It's enough to read the press... to understand the purposes of the exercises and how they disturb public opinion," he added.
On Tuesday several thousand pro-Communist demonstrators protested in Crimea's main city of Simferopol against unpaid wages, but also attacked Ukraine's current policy of close cooperation with NATO.
Meanwhile seven NATO ships will pay a goodwill visit to Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odessa later this week.
